At least when @60Minutes aired a short, edited version of its interview with Trump, it made the entire unedited video available online. But when @60Mins aired a highly edited interview with me that deliberately juxtaposed portions out of context, it refused to make the unedited interview available anywhere.

After I finally obtained a copy during discovery in the defamation lawsuit I won, 60 Minutes sought a restraining order to prevent me from posting the unedited video online. They told the judge that the public had no right to see the actual interview and should only see the deceptively edited portions they chose to air, which had already been ruled defamatory. 

After the judge warned them that forcing him to rule could harm the careers of Nick McKenzie and Charlotte Grieve, 60 Minutes dropped its request and agreed to pay my legal costs for the hearing. 

You can see both versions here. The defamatory version that 60 Minutes broadcast is second from the top, and the full, unedited interview is fourth from the top.

https://t.co/61ehWsel5z
